articles.title: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 Founders Edition Review - IGN
articles.summary: The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 is one of the most powerful (and expensive) graphics cards ever, and uses AI to further enhance its gaming performance.
articles.body:
Every couple of years, Nvidia launches an extremely expensive, extremely powerful graphics card that brings PC gaming into a new generation. That is what the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 ultimately is, but the way it brings next-generation performance is unconventional, to say the least. Because in a lot of games, the performance uplift over the RTX 4090 isn’t quite as steep as you’d expect – at least when DLSS Frame Generation is taken out of consideration. With the next generation of Nvidia’s DLSS for both upscaling and frame generation, however, we get leaps in image quality and performance that feel even greater than what we see with a typical graphics generation.

How much of an upgrade the Nvidia RTX 5090 is going to be for you, then, is ultimately going to depend on the games you play, the resolution you play those games at, and whether you’re ok with an AI algorithm generating extra frames. For a lot of people playing games on anything less than a 4K monitor with a 240Hz refresh rate, this upgrade is simply not going to make a lot of sense. But if you do have a high-end display, these AI-generated frames are going to feel like a taste of the future.

RTX 5090 too rich for you? Check out the RTX 5080 review.

The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 is built on Blackwell, Nvidia’s high-end architecture that’s already powering the data centers and supercomputers behind many of the most popular AI models. That should give you an idea of what the RTX 5090 is especially good at, but Nvidia didn’t neglect the, well, non-AI parts of the card.

With the 5090, Nvidia found a way to shove more Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) into the same amount of GPCs (Graphics Processing Clusters), which means more CUDA cores – 21,760, up from 16,384 in the RTX 4090. That makes up for a 32% uplift in the amount of shader cores over the previous generation, and is where a bulk of the raw gaming performance comes from.

Each SM also has four Tensor Cores and one RT Core, just like its predecessor. That means you get 680 Tensor Cores and 170 RT cores, compared to 512 and 128, respectively, for the RTX 4090 . The 5th-generation Tensor Cores are tailor-made to boost AI performance, with this generation adding support for FP4 operations, which should make AI workloads less dependent on VRAM.

All of this silicon is coupled with 32GB of GDDR7 VRAM, or video memory. This is a generational shift from the GDDR6X memory in the RTX 4090, and should be faster and more power efficient than the previous generation. But because the RTX 5090 requires a staggering 575W of power, a huge increase over the already power hungry 4090, power efficiency isn’t exactly Nvidia’s main goal with this graphics card.

Because the new Tensor Cores are more efficient, Nvidia shifted the entire DLSS algorithm to run on a Transformer Neural Network (TNN), rather than a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This shift won’t necessarily improve your framerate when you enable DLSS, but Nvidia claims it will improve image quality, and mitigate issues like ghosting and other unwanted artifacts.

Nvidia did more than just make an under-the-hood change to the way DLSS works. Team Green also introduces Multi-Frame Generation, which takes the Frame Gen tech introduced with the RTX 4090, makes it more efficient and smooth, and allows it to generate multiple frames off of each rendered image. This drastically improves frame rate, but should probably only be enabled if you’re already getting a decent frame rate, just like the last generation version.

The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 requires 575W of power, which is much more than the 450W of the RTX 4090. More power inherently means more heat, which means increasingly powerful cooling solutions are needed. Looking back at the RTX 4090 and even the RTX 3090 , the Founders Editions were these giant, triple-slot graphics cards that took up a ton of room, and straight up wouldn’t fit in some PC cases.

Before I saw the RTX 5090, I was expecting something even bigger and more unwieldy. However, somehow, it’s smaller. Nvidia was able to make a 575W graphics card fit in a dual-slot chassis with a dual fan configuration. And it works.

Throughout my time with the RTX 5090, which included both my standard testing suite and playing games with DLSS 4 enabled to test multi frame generation, the temperature maxed out at around 86°C, even while its power consumption peaked at 578W. That’s a high temperature, to be sure, and higher than the RTX 4090’s 80°C, but it’s not high enough to throttle, and that’s all that matters.

Nvidia was able to do this by shrinking down the PCB (printed circuit board) to a little square and placing it in the middle of the graphics card. The two fans are placed on each side of where the PCB is, with a heatsink that runs through the width of the card. These fans then take air in through the bottom of the card and shoot it straight through the top of the card and out through your exhaust fans in your PC case. In fact, this graphics card doesn’t even have exhaust vents under the output ports at the rear of the card, unlike previous generation designs.

But it’s immediately apparent that the RTX 5090 Founders Edition follows a similar design language to the last couple of generations. The center of the card has the same silver ‘X’ design as the RTX 4090, with a gunmetal-gray chassis surrounding the black heatsinks. On the outer edge of the graphics card, you get a ‘GeForce RTX’ logo that lights up with white LEDs, too.

Next to that logo, you’re going to find the power connector. While it looks very similar to the 12VHPWR connector of the last generation, it’s actually a new 12V-2x6 power connector. The difference is minor, but it’s supposedly more efficient than the last-generation connector. Maybe Nvidia will be available to avoid controversy around its power connectors melting with this generation – only time will tell.

Nvidia does include an 12V-2x6 adapter in the box, which takes four 8-pin PCIe power connectors in order to provide the required 575W of power. But what’s nice is that the connector on the graphics card itself is now angled, and facing the back of the graphics card, which should make connecting the cable much easier. The power connector seems more secure this time around, too.

The hidden benefit of this design is its ability to be slotted into smaller PC builds. You don’t need a giant case to run the RTX 5090, like you did with the RTX 4090 and 3090. However, it’s very likely that third-party designs from the likes of Asus and MSI are going to be much larger than Nvidia’s Founders Edition.

When Nvidia revealed the RTX 5090, it claimed that it could boost performance by as much as 8x. The actual number isn’t that high, but the RTX 5090 can deliver extremely high frame rates in the most demanding games, but not exactly through traditional rendering. Because while the RTX 5090 does deliver a decent increase in raw rasterization performance, the real next-generation benefit is in its ability to generate extra frames to increase your frame rate.

DLSS 4 introduces ‘Multi-Frame Generation’, a next-gen version of the Frame Generation introduced with DLSS 3 and the RTX 4090. But it’s more than just using the same method to just produce more frames. And the secret behind it is a new AI Management Processor, or AMP core in the RTX 5090 – along with other RTX 5000 graphics cards. The AMP allows the graphics card to essentially assign work to different parts of the GPU, something that was traditionally handled by your CPU. But because it’s physically located on the GPU, it’s able to do this much more efficiently.

According to Nvidia, the AMP and the 5th-generation Tensor Cores allowed it to create a new frame generation model that’s both 40% faster than the original frame generation model, while requiring 30% less memory. This new model only needs to run once on each rendered frame, which then can create 3 AI frames. Something like this would naturally introduce latency, but Nvidia found a way around that, too.

The AMP runs a Flip Metering algorithm, which paces out the frames in order to reduce input lag. Nvidia claims this is why multi-frame generation won’t work on RTX 4000 graphics cards, as the last-generation frame generation relied on the CPU for frame pacing, which would introduce much more latency than the new model, which runs entirely on the GPU itself.

To be clear, this isn’t a magic button to get good performance. Just like the previous generation, you only really want to enable this if you’re already getting a passable frame rate. If you’re not already getting around 60 fps with Frame Gen disabled, turning it on can introduce significant latency problems. That’s why it pairs best with DLSS upscaling also enabled, in order to maximise your performance.

When the RTX 5090 hits store shelves on January 30, DLSS 4 will work in a wide array of PC games that already support DLSS 3 Frame Generation. However, while working on this review, I only had access to two games with this technology enabled, and both were on beta builds – Cyberpunk 2077 and Star Wars Outlaws.

And I was surprised how well it worked. In Cyberpunk 2077 at 4K, on the Ray Tracing Overdrive Preset, with DLSS on Performance mode, the RTX 5090 gets 94 fps. That’s not bad for a game with full ray tracing. When I turned on DLSS 2x frame gen – the same as is supported by the RTX 4090 – that framerate increased to 162 fps. That’s a 2x improvement over just plain ol’ DLSS. However, when I cranked the frame generation to 4x, that’s 3 AI frames per rendered frame, that number went all the way up to 286 fps – more than my 4K display can actually render.

It’s a similar story with Star Wars Outlaws . Playing at 4K with all the settings cranked up to max, I was able to get up to around 300 fps with DLSS 4 enabled – and that’s up from about 120 fps without frame generation.

When I saw these framerates, I was straight-up expecting to see artifacts and weird spikes of lag. However, I only really saw one broken texture in Star Wars Outlaws, and it’s something I wouldn’t have noticed if I wasn’t actively looking for problems. It’s hard to believe, but Multi-Frame Generation actually does work, you just need to have an extremely high-end 4K display to benefit from it, at least with the RTX 5090.

It’s easy to write off this performance as ‘Fake Frames’, and you wouldn’t necessarily be wrong, especially because you need good baseline performance to make it a good experience. But it is going to be genuinely useful for anyone with a high-refresh, high-resolution display. It’s also important to keep in mind that I was only able to test it in a handful of games. Nvidia claims that 75 games will support DLSS 4 when the RTX 5090 hits store shelves on January 30, and there’s a decent possibility that it won’t work flawlessly in at least one of those games. For the time being, though, it looks like it works extremely well.

The Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 is an incredibly powerful graphics card, but testing this thing was a journey . In 3DMark, the RTX 5090 proved itself to provide a generational improvement over the RTX 4090 in terms of raw performance. However, things get a lot more complicated when I test actual games. In the vast majority of games, the RTX 5090 is bottlenecked by my CPU, even at 4K – and I paired it with the Ryzen 7 9800X3D , the fastest gaming processor on the market right now. For most people who already have a high-end graphics card, upgrading to this $1,999 GPU isn’t going to make a world of difference – the games just aren’t there yet. This is a graphics card you buy to set yourself up for future PC games, like The Witcher 4 .

I want to note that I did not enable DLSS 4 for any of these comparative benchmarks, and everything was tested on the public drivers available at the time. That means all non-5090 Nvidia cards were tested on Driver version 566.36, and all AMD cards were tested on AMD Adrenalin 24.12.1. All games were tested on their latest public builds, too.

In 3DMark, the RTX 5090 is up to 42% faster than the RTX 4090. In the Speed Way benchmark, the RTX 5090 scores 14,399 points to the RTX 4090’s 10,130, making for a 42% performance uplift. Similarly in Port Royal, the ray tracing test, the RTX 5090 scores 36,946 points to the 4090’s 25,997 points, which is also a 42% performance leap. What’s more impressive is how far Team Green has come since the RTX 3090. That graphics card got 5,619 points in Speed Way and 13,738 points in Port Royal, meaning anyone that skipped the last generation can get a 2.5x performance jump. That’s just 3DMark, though, and not necessarily reflective of real-world gaming performance.

In Call of Duty Black Ops 6 , however, we start to see the big issue with the RTX 5090 in today’s games – a severe CPU bottleneck. At 4K Extreme settings, with DLSS set to ‘performance’, the RTX 5090 gets 161 fps, compared to 146 fps from the RTX 4090. That’s just a 10% performance difference, and definitely not what I’d call a ‘next-generation’ performance increase. However, when looking back at the RTX 3090, the 4-year-old graphics card gets 91 fps, which means a nearly 2 x performance increase.

What’s wild is that the RTX 5090 even shows signs of CPU bottleneck in Cyberpunk 2077, one of the most demanding PC games on the market right now. At 4K, with the Ray Tracing Ultra preset and DLSS set to performance, the RTX 5090 gets 125 fps, compared to 112 fps from the RTX 4090 with the same settings. Similarly to Black Ops 6, this is just a 10% performance increase. That scaling just gets worse at lower resolutions, though, with the RTX 5090 getting 153 fps at 1440p and 156 fps at 1080p.

I test Metro Exodus: Enhanced Edition with DLSS disabled, because it’s the only upscaling solution in that game, and I need to get an honest comparison with AMD cards . This makes it one of the most demanding tests in my suite, and gives the RTX 5090 a chance to stretch its legs a bit. At 4K with the Extreme preset, the RTX 5090 gets 95 fps, compared to 76 fps from the RTX 4090 and 44 fps from the Radeon RX 7900 XTX. But even without the upscaling, the RTX 5090 only gets a 25% improvement over the RTX 4090, even if it more than doubles the 39 fps from the RTX 3090.

Red Dead Redemption 2 is getting up there in years, but it’s still a gorgeous game. At 4K with every setting maxed out, and DLSS set to performance mode, the RTX 5090 gets 167 fps, compared to 151 from the RTX 4090 and 92 fps from the RTX 3090. That means in this game, which admittedly doesn’t even use ray tracing, the RTX 5090 gets a paltry 6% performance uplift over the RTX 4090.

Total War: Warhammer 3 is an interesting test these days, because it doesn’t support ray tracing or upscaling, and gives a clear picture on raw rasterization performance. The RTX 5090 impresses here, delivering 147 fps to the RTX 4090’s 107 fps. That’s a 35% performance uplift and close to the potential performance difference demonstrated in 3DMark. However, it’s still a far cry from the 67% performance difference enjoyed by the RTX 4090 over the 3090.

Assassins Creed Mirage is a weird one. For some reason, when I first benchmarked this game, the RTX 5090 was getting terrible performance. Its game clock was limited to 772MHz, and was giving me around 50 fps at 4K. I was able to get around that problem, but even when it was resolved the 5090 only got 172 fps, which is lower than the RTX 4090 at 183 fps. What’s worse, is that the framerate was extremely spikey with microstutters. That’s bad, obviously, but it’s very likely that this is a driver bug, and as such should be treated as an outlier.

Black Myth: Wukong , like Cyberpunk 2077, is an extremely demanding game that will push any GPU to its limits. The RTX 5090, however, averaged 104 fps at 4K, with the Cinematic Preset and DLSS set to 40%. The RTX 4090, with identical settings, got 84 fps. That’s a 20% uplift in favor of the RTX 5090.

In Forza Horizon 5 , the RTX 5090 averaged 216 fps, compared to 210 fps from the RTX 4090, which is essentially in the margin of error. This is an aging game, to be sure, but the CPU bottleneck means there’s essentially no difference between these two cards at this resolution.

Nvidia really wants us to believe that Moore’s Law is dead and GPUs that deliver a giant uplift over their previous-generation counterparts are going to grow more rare over time. I don’t know if that’s true – I’m not an engineer – but regardless, in most games, the RTX 5090 doesn’t exactly deliver next-generation performance over the RTX 4090 – at least not to the extent that the latter card thoroughly trounced the 3090 back in 2022.

That’s not to say the RTX 5090 is a bad graphics card. No matter how you slice it, the RTX 5090 is now the fastest graphics card on the consumer market, and that’s not nothing . The problem is that a lot of games can’t really take advantage of the extra power offered by the Blackwell GPU. That’s something that will absolutely change over time, but it also means there’s little reason for someone with an RTX 4090 to upgrade to the new hotness.

Instead, the Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 is betting its existence on the future of AI-powered gaming. DLSS 4 uses AI to greatly increase frame rates, which is definitely a sight to behold. This graphics card is therefore best for gamers that want to be on the cutting edge, and are willing to bet $1,999 (at least) on an AI gaming future. For everyone else, the RTX 4090 is going to be more than powerful enough for the next few years.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Evento geek reúne dubladores, cosplay e games em Feira de Santana | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação terá painéis sobre cultura pop, concurso de cosplay e o Artists Alley no domingo (20).
articles.summary: Programação terá painéis sobre cultura pop, concurso de cosplay e o Artists Alley no domingo (20).
articles.body:
Evento geek será realizado em Feira de Santana neste fim de semana — Foto: Divulgação

A cidade de Feira de Santana , segunda maior da Bahia, recebe no domingo (20) o Comic Summit 2026, evento dedicado à cultura geek e pop. A programação será realizada das 8h às 18h, no Centro de Cultura Amélio Amorim, com atrações como dubladores, cosplay, games, RPG, TCG, Just Dance e estandes.

Com o tema “Novo universo!”, o evento terá entre os convidados os dubladores Ênio Vivona e Luísa Horta, além da atriz feirense Sara Barbosa.

Os ingressos custam a partir de R$ 30 e são vendidos pela internet, na plataforma sympla . Também haverá venda na porta do evento.

A programação começa pela manhã e segue até o fim da tarde, com atividades simultâneas em diferentes espaços.

Entre as opções estão partidas de TCG, jogos eletrônicos, batalhas de swordplay, RPG, Beyblade, experiências de realidade virtual e Just Dance.

Programação reúne dubladores, cosplay, games, RPG, TCG, Just Dance e estandes. — Foto: Divulgação

O evento também terá um Artists Alley, espaço dedicado a escritores, ilustradores e outros artistas independentes. A área está presente desde a primeira edição do Comic Summit e, neste ano, contará com nomes como Fabiana Cardeal, Douglas Amaral e Eri Amoedo.

No palco, a programação começa com a cerimônia de abertura. Ao longo do dia, estão previstos painéis sobre desenvolvimento de jogos, narrativas, cultura pop e cinema.

Entre os destaques estão o painel com Ênio Vivona, seguido de Meet & Greet com o dublador.

A programação ainda terá um concurso de cosplay, com o Cosplay Global Challenge e premiação.

Arena Pixel — Jogos eletrônicos: 8h30 às 17h

Arena Reinos — Swordplay/Batalha Campal: 8h30 às 17h

10h — Painel Conexões, com Bragi Estúdios

11h — Painel Narrativas, com Anderson Shon

12h30 — Painel Especial, com Mega Power Brasil

17h30 — Premiação do Cosplay Global Challenge

👾 Comic Summit 2026 📅 Data: 20 de setembro ⏰ Horário: das 8h às 18h 📍 Local: Centro de Cultura Amélio Amorim, Feira de Santana 🎟️ Ingressos: a partir de R$ 30, no sympla, com venda também na porta

articles.title: MTG Marvel Super Heroes Bundles Are Back in Stock on Amazon
articles.summary: Get Amazon discounts on Magic: The Gathering Marvel Super Heroes bundles, including the hard-to-find Gift Bundle with a Collector Booster.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering players will know all too well the struggle to find Collector Boosters when a set launches. These packs are pricey to begin with, but then scalpers complicate things. And since these are the best way to earn some of the rarest cards in a set, it’s bound to keep happening.

While we are starting to see Marvel Super Heroes Collector Boosters pop up a little more often, it’s not often we see a solid deal on a bundle that includes one. Thankfully, you can snag one such bundle for the set from Amazon right now at a slight discount.

Save 11% On This Bundle - Collector Booster Included

The Marvel Super Heroes Gift Edition Bundle is an ideal way to build a collection pretty quickly for anyone who’s keen on getting into Magic. The nice box doubles as storage, and you get nine Play Boosters inside.

There’s also an exclusive alternative art card exclusive to the bundle, and 30 land cards that include full-art, foil, and non-foil options, plus a special die.

Still, the real draw is undeniably the Collector Booster, which would make up almost half of the price of the box on its own. These cards are packed with rare cards and alternative art treatments, making them the best place to find the Marvel Super Heroes set’s most valuable cards .

The Gift Bundle isn’t the only one discounted, however. You can also grab a “fat pack” at a 25% discount from Amazon, bringing it down to $52.68 from $69.99 .

In this, you get a storage box, die, and an alternate art card, plus you get nine Play Boosters. In essence, you’re getting everything in the Gift Bundle, minus the Collector Booster, for almost $20 less.

If you’re only really after the rarer cards, the Collector Booster is undoubtedly the way to go, but if you’re happy to get nine packs to crack open and play with, this is a great way to go.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 — Everything Announced
articles.summary: Microsoft hit Tokyo Game Show 2026 with a special Xbox broadcast event, and IGN has a roundup of everything announced.
articles.body:
Microsoft's Tokyo Game Show 2026 Xbox broadcast is over, and we've got everything announced right here so you can catch up with all the news.

We got the campaign trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and confirmation that Mads Mikkelsen is in the game . We also got new trailers for Sega's Crazy Taxi World Tour, ArtPlay's Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement, and Atlus' Persona 4 Revival. I thought Raji: Kaliyuga looked pretty cool, too.

But the headline news here came from Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima, who provided development updates on OD and Physint, now both Xbox games. We have confirmation of the actor playing the lead role in Physint , and a cool first-look poster. Neither game has a release date yet.

If you need a catch-up, everything announced is below. And let us know what you're looking forward to in the comments!

Microsoft's TGS broadcast is over, and there was plenty in there for fans to get excited about. Let us know what you thought of the show in the comments.

Hideo Kojima did indeed turn up at the end of the Xbox broadcast to talk about Kojima Productions' partnership with Microsoft. He spoke about meeting new Xbox boss Asha Sharma to discuss the future of video games. As we know, Kojima is working on OD – KNOCK for Xbox, with production "proceeding on schedule." Expect more information "later down the line."

And Kojima mentioned Physint as a new Xbox game. He says it's the "culimation of more than 40 years of my career." It's making "steady progress," he added. Kojima also revealed the actor for the lead role... Bill Skarsgård! Expect more casting announcements in the future. "This has been Hideo Kojima," he signed off.

We got a fresh look at side-scrolling action game Bloodstained: The Scarlet Engagement during the show. ArtPlay revealed new gameplay from Koji Igarashi's new metroidvania, set in the gothic world of 16th Century England. The new trailer showcases the game’s fast-paced 2.5D action, with protagonists Leo and Alex battling their way through formidable enemies while exploring a sprawling, cursed land. Expect a release date in 2027.

We got a detailed look at Genigods: Nezha, an action RPG rooted in ancient Chinese genesis mythology from Genigods Lab, coming out in 2028. Here's the official blurb:

Genigods: Nezha is an ARPG rooted in the chaos of ancient Chinese creation mythology. Play as Spirit Pearl, the first being forged by the Goddess of Creation Nüwa. Dive into iconic Chinese genesis tales, battle Colossal Gods, and experience the unique combat of Chinese-style celestial showdowns.

Midgar Studios' Edge of Memories got a new trailer. This is another French studio's take on the JRPG genre, and it's due out November 5, 2026.

Developed through a collaboration between a small French studio and veteran Japanese developers, this gorgeous anime-style world is threatened by a mysterious disease that corrupts the land as you progress through the story, opening new paths in areas you’ve already explored.

Join Eline and her companions on a journey to stop the spread of the Corrosion and save their home. The latest trailer showcases the Japanese dub, featuring a cast of renowned Japanese voice actors. Whether you’re playing in English or Japanese, pre-order Edge of Memories now on Xbox Series X and S.

Once Human: Isles of Abyss got a release date reveal trailer. The free-to-play "strange worlds survival game" releases the Isles of Abyss expansion on October 22 on Xbox Series X and S with full cross-play. Once Human is already available now with Xbox Game Pass.

I thought Raji: Kaliyuga was one of the standout games from Xbox's TGS broadcast. The developer commentary video, from Indian studio Nodding Heads Games, focused on gameplay and gave us a good look at what to expect from combat. Raji: Kaliyuga features dual protagonists: Raji, with acrobatic martial arts and the Trishul, and Darsh, with immense Siddhi powers that control gravity, time, and energy. It introduces customized evasion for Raji and a siddhi-yielding system for Darsh, allowing unique combat styles. The game shifts from an isometric action-adventure to a third-person action-adventure.

Raji: Kaliyuga is coming to Xbox Series X and S and Xbox on PC as an Xbox Play Anywhere title and with Xbox Game Pass. Certainly one to watch.

Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories

Koei Tecmo showed a new trailer for Atelier Karia: The Night Kingdom & the Guide of Memories, due out in February. It confirms the return of Rutger and Lenja from Atelier Yumia. Now experienced members of the Aladiss Pioneering Team, the two support Karia and her companions on their new adventure, with their interactions with new companions revealing new sides of both returning characters.

Atelier Karia tells the story of Karia, who has no memories, as she faces her past. New features add to the strategy of battles and depth of alchemy. Synthesized items take on new roles during exploration, and ingredients can be eaten to gain effects.

We got a world premiere! Serenity Forge, the publisher of Vivarium, revealed surreal sci-fi adventure Faraday Blues. The game is three interconnected visual novels about a daughter searching for parents who don’t know she exists. It's coming to Xbox Series X and S and PC in 2027, with Xbox Cloud support.

Studio Ghibli-inspired cozy crafting adventure Bloomwalker is "joining the Ni no Kuni universe," Xbox has confirmed. Players travel with a moving house to cleanse the pollution spreading across the land, restoring its sanctuaries and freeing its guardians. It's coming to Xbox Series X and S and Xbox on PC.

We got an extended look at Lofty Sky's Hope in the City. Here's the official description:

17-year-old Hope Song thought the national exams were her biggest worry... until she got home to a ransacked apartment and two missing parents. Investigate through the eyes of an artist, turn sketches into evidence, and watch her family's mystery grow stranger and darker with every answer.

Hope in the City is a narrative mystery game played through the eyes of an artist: investigate, turn sketches into evidence, and watch your family's mystery grow stranger and darker with every answer. Hope in the City comes to Xbox Series X and S, Xbox on PC, and Game Pass on November 10, 2026, with Xbox Play Anywhere support.

Wo Long 2: Wings of Ember turned up with a fresh look at combat and the reveal of a boss fight. A demo is out now. The full game is coming March 4, 2027, and will be on Game Pass.

Shape of Dreams, a co-op action roguelite, is available today for Xbox Series X and S and is day one with Xbox Game Pass. The Xbox version launches alongside the game’s first anniversary update, The Starless Path, which adds a new Traveler, a new final boss, and a new ending.

Persona 4 Revival got a new trailer, showing off a brief look at Atlus' game. It's due out next year, and is coming to Game Pass.

oh hey Detective Prince 🕵️​ ​ meet who you'll be solving cases with in Persona 4 Revival | #XBOXTokyoGameShow pic.twitter.com/5y9RwDNueC — XBOX Game Pass (@XBOXGamePass) September 17, 2026

oh hey Detective Prince 🕵️​ ​ meet who you'll be solving cases with in Persona 4 Revival | #XBOXTokyoGameShow pic.twitter.com/5y9RwDNueC

As expected, Xbox showed a new trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, which is set in Korea, among other places. The campaign video sets up iconic hero Captain Price as the target this time. A face-off with Ghost is inevitable. And we also have confirmation that Mads Mikkelsen is in the game!

The official Campaign trailer for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is now live. It digs deep into the story, centered on John Price's shadow operations, including conflict with former allies and alliances with a former foe. Experience the invasion of South Korea and the threat of a weapon that could overturn the world order in the hands of the villainous Archer.

Sega showed off a look at Japan in Crazy Taxi World Tour, coming out next year. "Japan: A place beautifully suspended between two worlds," reads the official description. "Here, historic neighborhoods and tradition sit alongside the bustling energy of the modern city. Get ready to fall in love with the land of the rising sun when Crazy Taxi: World Tour hits the streets in 2027!"

articles.title: Hot Wheels Infinite Rush Video Review - IGN
articles.summary:
Hot Wheels Infinite Rush reviewed by Luke Reilly on PC. Also available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Switch 2.
"It’s fair to say that taking the miniaturised motoring mayhem that Milestone established in its Hot Wheels Unleashed games and reinventing it in an open-world format sounds like a slam dunk on paper. Hot Wheels Infinite Rush’s racing does remain robust and approachable, with difficulty levels tuned for both total beginners and arcade racing experts. There’s also a generous amount of activities to complete if you’re so inclined, and a huge pile of Hot Wheels models to collect – all of which look as fabulously photo-realistic as ever. It’s continued embrace of powerful customisation tools that allow us to create our own bonkers tracks and cool, one-off cars is also great; it adds a lot of lasting value and it’s reverent to the DNA of this whole hobby. Unfortunately, Infinite Rush is now missing most of its charm and character following the transition to an open world, and it’s easily the least compelling Hot Wheels game out of Milestone to date. With unmemorable pre-built tracks and bland maps that completely lack the sense of scale we get in the life-sized, real-world environments of the Unleashed games, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush has sadly lost a ton of its toy-like personality – and that just can’t be fixed with a large plastic gorilla or octopus."

articles.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Expected to Break Franchise Box Office Record, Topping 2010's Resident Evil: Afterlife
articles.summary: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is expected to make more money at the box office on opening weekend than any other Resident Evil movie before it.
articles.body:
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil is expected to make more money at the box office on opening weekend than any other Resident Evil movie before it.

Resident Evil: Afterlife currently holds the domestic opening weekend box office record for the franchise, with $26.6 million back in 2010 (not adjusted for inflation). Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil, according to Variety , is targeting $40-50 million, but some believe it could end up near $60 million.

Deadline reports Resident Evil is expected to add $31 million overseas for a global total of around $80 million. Given Sony reportedly spent $75 million producing the movie (not including marketing spend), $80 million would be a fantastic start. Cregger brings with him added interest due to his past work on breakout horror movies, including Weapons. Sony will be hoping for more of the same with Resident Evil.

Upcoming New Video Game Movies and TV Shows: 2026 Release Dates and Beyond

Afterlife, by the way, ended up with $300 million globally from theaters, so Cregger and co certainly have their work cut out topping that. Resident Evil: The Final Chapter — the last of the Paul W. S. Anderson / Milla Jovovich Resident Evil movies — ended with $312 million globally in 2017. It is currently the highest grossing Resident Evil movie.

IGN’s Resident Evil review returned an 8/10. We said: “With a laser focus on putting its hero through the worst night of his life, Resident Evil is a simple and exciting survival horror story that benefits greatly from director Zach Cregger’s sensibilities.”

The movie’s apparent inevitable success comes despite deep-rooted skepticism from some Resident Evil fans who wanted a more faithful adaptation of the video games. Cregger himself has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating this skepticism , which began when it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes .

Cregger recently told IGN’s Tom Jorgensen : “I think I was naive. I thought fans of these games, like me, would be thrilled that somebody was coming along and turning Resident Evil into a survival horror movie. I was like, ‘That’s great.’ I did not really appreciate the sentiment that, ‘We’ve been waiting forever for Leon’s story.’ And I appreciate that, and I’m sorry that’s not the story I’m bringing. I get it, I understand the frustration. I understand it so well because I haven’t seen the earlier [Resident Evil] movies, because they don't look like the Resident Evil that I love, so how could I be frustrated with fans who have that same attitude?”

“My only hope is that they’ll see the movie regardless of their skepticism or their disappointment that I’m not telling some of the stories that the games tell so well, and they will feel seen when they do watch the movie, and they will recognize all of the love for the games that are in this movie, because it is there,” he continued.

“This is not me just telling a story and slapping Resident Evil on it so I can get a budget. This is me telling a Resident Evil story. I understand the resistance, I do, because I have it myself. It is coming from a true place of love.”

Last week, Cregger revealed he cut most of the jokes in Resident Evil , after test audiences apparently found the film "too funny." Cregger has also revealed who he'd cast as Lady Dimitrescu if he ever got the chance.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima Announces It Star Bill Skarsgard Will Portray Physint's Main Character
articles.summary: It star Bill Skarsgard will portray Physint's main character, Hideo Kojima has just confirmed.
articles.body:
It star Bill Skarsgård will portray Physint's main character, Hideo Kojima has just announced, days after the bombshell revelation that PlayStation had walked away from the project, which will now be published by Xbox instead .

Skarsgård will play Physint's unnamed lead character and protagonist, and joins the previously announced trio of actors on the project: Charlee Fraser, Don Lee and Minami Hamabe. While still years from release, Kojima said today that Physint was continuing to making "steady progress."

Behind the scenes footage of Physint's early production premiered during today's Xbox Tokyo Game Show 2026 broadcast. A poster for the game has also revealed its tagline: "The Next Cold War Begins."

"I'm delighted to confirm the lead role for Physint will be Bill Skarsgård,” Kojima said today. "We are both long-time fans of each other's work, and we've decided to embark on this new adventure together. The costume fittings, scans, and camera tests we conducted with Bill and Charlee earlier this year gave me tremendous confidence in the direction of the project. My vision of the final form became much more solidified."

Skarsgård is best known for playing creepy clown Pennywise in It, It: Chapter Two, and It: Welcome to Derry. He's also appeared in Nosferatu, Barbarian, The Crow, and John Wick: Chapter 4, as well as TV series such as Castle Rock and Hemlock Grove.

"Physint is the culmination of more than 40 years of my career," Kojima added, "a project that will redefine 'action-espionage', unbound by any existing genres in digital entertainment. The project conitnues to make steady progress. We're also making progress on casting, talent scans, and collaborations with outside creators. There are still many exciting cast announcements to come in future, so please stay tuned for further updates.

"Finally, I would liek to sincerely thank all of our players, fans, and community members for tuning in and for your continued support. I would also like to thank our partners at Xbox for believing in our vision and walking this parth toward the future alongside us. We are incredibly excited about the road ahead and look forward to sharing much more with you in the future. Please stay tuned!"

Last week, it was reported that Sony ditched Kojima due to budget concerns and missed deadlines on Physint , which is in development to arrive after the Metal Gear Solid creator's other upcoming project, OD. Analysts speculated that lower sales of Death Stranding's sequel may also have played a part in spooking PlayStation , though others suggested that publishing Kojima games has always been about more than just raw sales figures.

articles.title: Hot Wheels Infinite Rush Review
articles.summary: With unmemorable tracks and maps that completely lack the sense of scale we get in the life-sized, real-world environments of the Unleashed games, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush has sadly shed a ton of the series' special charm.
articles.body:
Giving the modern Hot Wheels racing series a radical, Burnout Paradise-inspired overhaul sounds like a pretty fabulous idea when you say it aloud. That Criterion Games classic is, after all, one of the most revered arcade racers in the business – even if it was ultimately the last proper Burnout we ever got. Unfortunately, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush has sacrificed far, far too much of what makes developer Milestone’s initial pair of Hot Wheels Unleashed games so eye-catching, zany, and special. Infinite Rush’s four modestly sized maps weave familiar bits and pieces of plastic track through otherwise unmemorable slabs of landscape and basic city blocks, and they totally lack the scope and spectacle of the Unleashed series’ life-sized skate parks, construction sites, and neon arcades. The racing may be fine and functional, but Infinite Rush is disappointingly basic and bland compared to its existing brethren, so it’s difficult to recommend over either of them.

Hot Wheels Infinite Rush is instantly recognisable as a Milestone Hot Wheels game thanks to its unmatched ability to present these car models in an uncannily photorealistic way. The cars still broadly look fantastic. From zinc to plastic, the surfaces of every model gleam with authenticity and – despite the fact it’s been this way since the first one arrived in 2021 – it still remains thoroughly impressive to me how terrific they look on screen. They just look real .

Unfortunately, they no longer appear to accumulate wear and tear like they did in the Milestone’s earlier games. Upon reaching the end of a race, my cars now look just as factory fresh as they did when I started. The scratches, rubs, scuffed plastic, and kerb rash that builds up on cars in the Unleashed games is a big part of what pumps up their credibility; that is, making the cars look and feel like they’ve just tumbled down the driveway a dozen times really seats them into the maps and makes them look like actual play-worn toys. In contrast, Hot Wheels Infinite Rush feels glossy and consequence-free. Am I missing something here? A hidden setting? Was this an intentional change for Infinite Rush for some unknown reason, or a licensor change-of-heart? Whatever it was, it’s a really weird step back and I’m not a fan.

It appears about one-third of the options that make up the roughly 150-car roster are new, rather than recycled. This is welcome, as it certainly doesn’t make much sense to keep wheeling out the same cars when there are almost 60 years of Hot Wheels castings to choose from. That said, the garage is still weighted very heavily towards new and recent models. There’s a decent smattering of early to mid-2000s castings, including AcceleRacers, but there’s really nothing here for Gen X parents or grandparents to share with younger players. The ’70s, ’80s, and ’90s remain woefully underrepresented. I get that older players aren’t really the primary audience of a licensed Hot Wheels game, but I know that my sons’ Hot Wheels collection is like a core sample of Hot Wheels history. It’s got recent cars, my childhood cars, and old cars from their uncles – and even great uncle. I get the feeling that’s probably a pretty common occurrence. The balance in Infinite Rush is just… off. There are definitely times it feels like it was more important for this to be a catalogue of cars kids can still see at the shops rather than a rummage through the toyline’s past.

Infinite Rush is also missing the pop culture cars that were fixtures in the Unleashed games. The fact that it features Ferrari is neat enough, considering the Prancing Horse’s decade-long absence from the real-life Hot Wheels line-up from 2015 to 2025, but the lack of any movie or TV cars feels a bit cheap.

Infinite Rush uses a similar class system for the cars as Unleashed 2, although it dials it back to four distinct classes rather than six: Versatile, Speeder, Drifter, and Titan. Each has nuances you need to cater for as you drive. For instance, Titans are strong but bulky – and they have extra long boost meters to compensate. However, run your boost all the way down to zero and your default speed will be strangled momentarily as your engine coughs back to life. Versatile racers have a drift bar that’s consumed in chunks, meaning you can’t stop a boost once you’ve started. It means they’re not a great fit for navigating the urban, grid-like portions of the maps, because it can be hard to force them into the right direction when in the middle of a briefly unstoppable boost.

Drifters are my preferred class, since they’re the easiest to sling sideways and therefore the best fit for an arcade racing game. The other classes are less satisfying to drift, and there sometimes seems as if there’s even a bit of a speed penalty for doing so. There were definitely occasions it was overtly faster to Hail Melon around a corner, Ross Chastain-style, than it was to slide into it properly. This shouldn’t really be the case in any arcade racer.

Rank these open-world racing and driving games

The biggest problem with Infinite Rush is how surprisingly generic the open-world approach makes it feel. It doesn’t have a single, large open map to explore like, say, Burnout Paradise or Forza Horizon 6. Instead, there are four separate, modestly sized islands – each themed in slightly different ways. There’s Wheelswood, a commercial-style, downtown-inspired map; Tentacle Bay, another city-oriented environment, only with a little more open countryside; Gearville, a desert-themed, industrial zone; and Drifty Temples, an East Asian-inspired island. I just find myself blazing through them, smashing through bushes and benches. There’s some decent imagination on display – and I do think the huge Hot Wheels Mount Rushmore on Gearville is pretty cute – but broadly speaking there’s just not much that grabs my attention. Not even the big, plastic animals.

In the Unleashed games, you find yourself racing through half-built skyscrapers above the clouds – or staring up at enormous arcade cabinets, which might as well be skyscrapers themselves with the way they loom over your tiny toy cars, from down on the sticky carpet. Infinite Rush has absolutely none of this scale, and it’s all the worse for it. They’re not quite believable dioramas, even if they’re filled with moulded plastic props. But they’re not quite real places either – even if the default measure of distance to my next waypoint is metres. 800 metres away, in a car that’s ostensibly three inches long? Something’s not adding up.

In a word, these maps are bland. You just drive back and forth across them, competing in a genre-typical range of event types. The racing is still fine, although the tracks are nowhere near as interesting anymore because they simply can’t use their surroundings in the same way as the Unleashed games can. There you can race on the floors, across the furniture, up in the air vents – you name it. Infinite Rush has none of that. Worse, a lot of the side activities that appear to be here to justify these open-world maps are just busywork – like photograph challenges that tell you exactly where to take them, or checkpoint collections that’d be a lot less trivial to complete if you actually had to dodge traffic (which you don’t; smashing through them doesn’t even really slow you down).

There was probably a way to experiment and take the series to an open world without sacrificing the sense of scale Unleashed got so right. Could the desert map have been built on a beach, or one of the other maps laid out in the foyer of a toy store? Anything like this would’ve given the backdrops the scale Infinite Rush lacks. Could more of the architecture have been household objects, with cereal box buildings standing side by side with Hot Wheels garage playsets, and painted roads filling the gaps between the iconic orange track pieces? I just feel like there was a more imaginative way to tackle this shift. 2023’s LEGO 2K Drive did this approach better overall, but unfortunately that game is already completely delisted in digital stores.

The profound shift in map philosophy is doubly disappointing considering the improvements Infinite Rush makes elsewhere. For instance, it now comes with four-player splitscreen, which would’ve been amazing fun in the massively more imaginative Unleashed maps. It also now features the ability for AI to race on your custom tracks, which would’ve been another huge boost to longevity for the older games. I would’ve loved to have seen how the AI handled the wild leaps of the crazy routes I’ve created in the past (especially since Infinite Rush is way, way more restrictive in terms of the height limit than the Unleashed games – which feature multi-level maps with a ton of vertical space). Infinite Rush also features the new ability to change out wheels as part of the customisation suite, which speaks to me as a 40-odd-year-old diorama-building dork who loves swapping out wheels on his Hot Wheels cars. Okay, they’re not always mine, but my boys aren’t using them anymore; just don’t tell them I’ve been attacking their collection with a power drill.

articles.title: The Grand Tour Reboot Season 1 Review
articles.summary: The new Grand Tour is a fun and ambitious attempt to prove that the format can soldier on without the much-loved line up that previously helmed it and, perhaps against all odds, it has honestly succeeded.
articles.body:
All six episodes of season 1 of The Grand Tour’s new series are available to watch now on Prime Video.

At the peak of its power, The Grand Tour became Prime Video’s most-watched unscripted UK original series globally, but the show’s been up on the hoist since September 2024, when original hosts Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May took their final bow in the episode “One for the Road.” It marked the last trip for the trio after 22 years of working together on The Grand Tour and the BBC’s Top Gear. 2026’s new vision of The Grand Tour – hosted by Thomas Holland, James Engelsman, and Francis Bourgeois – is an ambitious attempt to prove that the format can soldier on without the much-loved line up that previously helmed it. Perhaps against all odds, it has mostly succeeded.

The new series’ opening moments see an awestruck new trio share a moment with Jeremy Clarkson on his Diddly Squat Farm, which is a brief sketch setting Clarkson up as something closer to a head of state than an elder peer. It’s a cute if slightly clunky bit, but it’s a smart springboard for the new series; they may be restarting from “Season 1” as far as their presence on Prime Video is concerned, but the new Grand Tour is not ignoring the series’ history. In this way, it becomes less of a reboot and more of a relay; they’re just picking up the baton and carrying on. “Seriously, have fun with this,” says Clarkson as they depart, in probably the one part of the encounter that genuinely feels off the cuff. “I mean it, and good luck. And don’t f–k it up.”

The basic formula of the show remains intact – a mix of bespoke themed segments and long-form road trips (in this instance, across parts of the US, Malaysia, and Angola). If there’s been a noteworthy reduction in budget since the departure of the original hosting trio, it’s certainly not visible on screen. The vehicle footage remains sumptuously shot, and there’s no skimping on the execution of expensive ideas, whether that’s using a giant airbag to fling an unwanted Tesla through the air and destroy it, or a hypercar race involving three jets and a £2.1 million, 2,031 brake horsepower Hennessey Venom F5 Revolution Evolution.

The Grand Tour New Series - Season 1 Photos

What’s perhaps most pleasing is the immediate rapport between all three hosts. Admittedly, Holland and Engelsman arrive from well-established YouTube motoring channel Throttle House, where their chemistry has already been developed through years of video content. It means that they’re not only comfortable in front of a camera discussing cars, they’re also comfortable disagreeing with each other, and their unplanned exchanges typically seem like credible banter between mates. Bourgeois is particularly surprising; as the one member of the new trio who doesn’t come from a motoring journalism background, his inclusion was hard to figure out in the lead-up to his debut. I’m unfamiliar with his social media schtick because I’ve never used TikTok, but his enthusiasm for his new role is utterly infectious and he seems extremely knowledgeable. The show certainly leans into his established social media fascination with trains, but he knows cars too. He’s a truly interesting fellow who communicates with the quietly spoken authority of someone twice his age, but he can flip a switch and become a buzzing teenager behind the wheel… and he’s highly watchable as both.

If you want a quick taste of Bourgeois’ presenting style, you can dip in to the opening segment of Episode 4, where he and Holland pit two hideously expensive restomods against one another: a Totem GT Super (reimagining the classic Alfa Romeo GTA) and the Prodrive P25 (a half-a-million pound remake of the absolutely legendary Subaru Impreza 22B). As an absolute sucker for ’90s rally cars, I couldn’t help but share Bourgeois’ deep admiration for the P25, and the fact that it was introduced with one of the strongest needle drops I’ve heard in the show’s history didn’t hurt. One of the best rock bangers of the ’90s to celebrate one of the baddest four-bangers ever unleashed on gravel? Yes, please! It’s actually a segment they could’ve done a bit more with, considering how much the concept of restomods mirrors what’s happening with this new season. Taking a recognizable classic and updating it with new, modern internals? The script would’ve almost written itself.

Prior to the debut of the new series, Thomas Holland admitted that after hearing The Grand Tour was being rebooted without Clarkson, Hammond, or May, he quipped: “Only a moron would take that job.” The sentiment has clear precedent. For many years, the BBC’s Top Gear tried to establish a line-up of replacement hosts for the programme after Clarkson was axed and Hammond, May, and producer and co-creator Andy Wilman subsequently followed him out the door. Top Gear then saw eight different hosts from 2016 up until the show was put on ice in 2023. It became fascinated by filling the roster with sitcom stars, cricket players, and F1 team founders, and it never rediscovered the proper formula. It’s early days, but I think The Grand Tour has.

Set to launch on PlayStation 5 at some point in 2027, this long-awaited sequel features more fast-paced undead slicing, and even more of its plucky heroine Juliet, who appears to be wearing an even shorter skirt.

The original Lollipop Chainsaw debuted in 2012, and found cult status. It featured a witty script, partly penned James Gunn (before his days making Marvel and DC movies), and was the overall brainchild of Suda51, the legendary Japanese creator behind No More Heroes, Shadows of the Damned and a slew of other offbeat ideas.

15 years on, however, neither Gunn or Suda51 are contributing to this sequel. Instead, it is the work of Dragami Games, which previously released a remaster of the original Lollipop Chainsaw to a mixed response. Today's footage has also sparked a range of reactions on social media, where many have suggested that this sequel looks unpolished.

Lollipop Chainsaw 2 Back2Back has been announced for PS5 and a gameplay video has been released! It will launch in 2027 pic.twitter.com/qXiwOhRW6V

"Juliet returns, in a brand-new outfit and with even more power, to a rebuilt San Romero, now transformed into 'Jaredwood,' a sprawling metropolis built around the film industry," reads a blurb for the new game. When a mysterious director traps her inside his twisted zombie movie, Juliet must fight alongside her allies, uncover the conspiracy behind the chaos, and stop a new threat posed by the Corrupted Realm zombies."

Footage revealed today as part of Tokyo Games Show 2026 featured Juliet slicing up zombies on a street, where her new rollerskates allow her to zip about at a faster speed. Further footage revealed a boss battle against Zorbie, a zombie that appears to be a riff on Barbie.

Last year, a Lollipop Chainsaw anime series was also announced as being in development . There's no further word on that today.

articles.title: Twitch Boss Says Game Companies Are Right to Avoid Competing With GTA 6 for Attention — Expects GTA Online 2 Next Year
articles.summary: Twitch boss Dan Clancy has said he expects an enormous launch for GTA 6 this November, one video game companies are right to avoid like the plague. But he also expects GTA 6 to continue to hoover up the internet’s attention when GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called —  launches next year.
articles.body:
Twitch boss Dan Clancy has said he expects an enormous launch for GTA 6 this November, one video game companies are right to avoid like the plague. But he also expects GTA 6 to continue to hoover up the internet’s attention when GTA Online 2 — or whatever GTA 6’s multiplayer mode is called — launches next year.

Speaking to Bloomberg , Clancy said he’d spoken with Rockstar Games about what the developer has up its sleeve.

“We spent a lot of time talking with Rockstar about their plans, and also helping them think about how they can engage our creators,” Clancy said. “You are going to see this big bump with GTA 6, but then an even bigger one next year when they launch multiplayer.”

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Rockstar is yet to say when the multiplayer portion of GTA 6 will come out, or even confirm it plans to release a GTA Online 2, even though everyone knows it’s in the works. There is intense speculation about when it will release, or, more specifically, how long Rockstar will wait to deploy it after GTA 6’s November release date. Early 2027? Mid 2027? Late 2027? Either way, next year looks nailed on.

Will GTA Online 2 make the existing GTA Online redundant? Not necessarily. Last year, Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, said Take-Two has form when it came to NBA 2K Online, a free-to-play online-focused version of 2K Sports’ hugely successful basketball franchise aimed at the Asian market. NBA 2K Online launched all the way back in 2012, and then 2K Sports released NBA 2K Online 2 in 2017. Both games were maintained simultaneously, so fans of the first version could continue to play and invest their time and money safe in the knowledge they wouldn’t be left behind.

“I'm going to speak theoretically only because I'm not going to talk about a particular project when an announcement hasn't been made,” Zelnick told IGN . “But generally speaking, we support our properties when the consumers are involved with those titles. As an example, we launched NBA 2K Online in China, I think originally in 2012 if I'm not mistaken. And then we launched NBA 2K Online 2 in China in 2017. If I'm not mistaken. We did not sunset Online 1. They both are still in the market and they serve consumers and they're alive and we have this massive audience.

“So we've shown a willingness to support legacy titles when a community wants to be engaged with them.”

That last line is of particular importance. It suggests — but doesn’t confirm at this stage — that if there is a GTA Online 2, it won’t come at the cost of GTA Online falling by the wayside. If people keep playing GTA Online, Zelnick is suggesting here, then Rockstar will continue to support it. And let's remember, GTA 6 launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S only. PC players' only option is to join the console party, or stick with GTA 5 and GTA Online on PC.

With November fast approaching, Rockstar has begun to reveal more about GTA 6 and how it will play. Just this week a number of artists teased their appearance on the GTA 6 soundtrack , and Stephen Root, who voices Bill Dauterive and Buck Strickland on the animated series King of the Hill, confirmed his role in the GTA 6 cast .

Remarkably, Rockstar has yet to confirm any GTA 6 actors, leading fans to try to work out the cast for themselves. We don’t even know who plays Jason and Lucia, the game’s dual protagonists. Perhaps we won’t until the game is out in November and the credits roll.

While you wait to find out, check out IGN’s extensive GTA 6 coverage, including our interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson on what to expect .

articles.title: GTA 6 Soundtrack Gets Physical CD and Vinyl Release, Rockstar Confirms
articles.summary: Rockstar will launch a physical edition of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack, a new leak has revealed.
articles.body:
Rockstar will launch a $125 physical edition of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack, available on limited edition vinyl.

The news was broken this afternoon by the ever-reliable billbil-kun at Dealabs , while Rockstar announced the soundtrack itself a few minutes later. The collection of music will be published by Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records on November 19 — the same day as GTA 6 hits digital game stores.

A double LP vinyl edition will be sold for $50, while a double CD version will sell for $20. For collectors, though, there's the limited edition vinyl set which contains "two transparent magenta discs filled with blue liquid," plus exclusive artwork. This is the one you'll pay $125 for. All editions are available for preorder now.

This news is somewhat ironic, considering the fact that GTA 6 itself will not get a physical launch on a disc , something that has sparked complaints from fans who want to own an actual copy of the upcoming blockbuster rather than an empty box.

Today's announcement follows a spate of teases by music streaming service Spotify both online and across billboards in New York, Los Angeles, and Miami. The teases continued online via the social media accounts of an array of artists, including Travis Scott and Keith Richards , that suggested they were also involved somehow with GTA 6. Now, we know why.

Travis Scott and Keith Richards are among the first batch of artists confirmed to have contributed music to the new album, with more tracks to be announced. Spotify will be one of the many places to stream the soundtrack online, meanwhile.

Indeed, Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album is now available for pre-save via major streaming services , where you can also listen to the first six tracks.

articles.title: South Park May Be Called South America Now, but the Series Succeeds in Returning to its Roots in the Season 29 Premiere
articles.summary: South Park kicks off Season 29 and the new South America era by delivering an episode that feels like a return to the shows' roots in the best way.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for South Park Season 29, Episode 1!

Part of the fun with each new season of South Park is seeing where the series directs its attention after being off the air for months (sometimes years). It's not as if there's any shortage of big news and topical headlines worth lampooning right now. And the show certainly made a strong impression right out of the gate in last year's Season 27 premiere . That's why it's a little surprising to see Season 29 take a very different approach in its premiere episode. Despite a few nods to current events, this is very much a classic-style episode. And honestly, it makes for a nice change of pace.

Obviously, the series has hardly moved on from lampooning the actions of the Trump administration in Season 29. It's right there in the decision to change the title to "South America." And it seems safe to assume South America is going to increasingly lean into political humor as we get closer to the November midterms (and the release of GTA VI). But for now, we get an episode that really plays like a throwback to the early seasons of the show. The focus shifts back to Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny. Randy is out there being a solipsistic doofus. The episode even climaxes with Kenny dying for the first time in however many years it's been. It really is a blast from the past in many ways.

For the most part, that classical approach works well here. I do think the climax of the episode is a little rushed and unsatisfying. But for the most part, it really is a refreshing change of pace to see Stan and the gang in the spotlight again and for the show to pivot away from trying to be as superhumanly timely as possible. Cartman tends to steal the spotlight here, as his sheer glee over the freedom granted by being an obnoxious e-bike rider is pretty hilarious. I also got a big kick out of Cartman's interview scene, where his secret identity wasn't particularly well hidden.

This was definitely Cartman and Randy's week to shine. With Randy, it's just so nice to finally be rid of the played-out Tegridy Farms shtick and onto something new. It really works seeing Randy suddenly recast as a weed-hating, cycling-obsessed health nut who looks down his nose at the kids and their newfangled e-bikes. And it's only fitting that this episode takes that new role to its extreme, leading to Randy forming a violent South American biker gang that pays off the police and delivers the heads of their enemies to the mayor. I can only wonder where this strange new journey will take Randy over the course of Season 29.

It's also worth mentioning that the City Wok owner, Lu Kim, plays a pretty great supporting role here. His business has transformed yet again (though we get a fun nod to Season 27's Labubu fad on the signage), this time focusing on peddling City E-Bikes and Super City E-Bikes. The premiere's musical game is also very on-point. Not only does Brad Paisley contribute that catchy little country music ditty that closes out the episode, but Trey Parker and Matt Stone even brought in Primus to re-record the intro song for this new South America era.

On that note, the title change serves to anchor this episode to the current political climate. This is South Park's way of eviscerating Trump's habit of unilaterally renaming geopgraphic landmarks and of corporations like Apple and Google simply rolling over and embracing the name changes. As much as I'm concerned this gag is going to grow stale really quickly in Season 29, it is pretty funny to watch the news reporter take the townspeople to task for capitulating. We'll see how well this joke holds up in the coming weeks.

articles.title: MTG Arena Commander Is "Being Worked On", but Not Coming Anytime Soon
articles.summary: Wizards of the Coast has confirmed 4-player Commander is in development for MTG Arena, but design challenges mean players shouldn't expect it anytime soon.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering is playable in a variety of formats, but one has taken on a life of its own. Commander is inarguably the game’s most popular way to play, and Wizards of the Coast has wisely leaned into it with preconstructed decks that make it easier to play with friends with minimal deckbuilding (although that’s always an option, too).

Still, Commander isn’t supported by Wizards of the Coast, leading to players getting their digital fix for it via alternatives like Tabletop Simulator. As the game (and Commander itself) grow in popularity, however, it appears that may change soon.

Commander is Magic’s premier multiplayer format, meaning it eschews the traditional 1v1 style of play. It’s playable with anywhere from three players to a dozen (or more), and revolves around 100-card decks where only basic lands can be included multiple times.

Players build their decks around a ‘Commander’, a card that essentially helms the deck and offers a unique playstyle that other cards work to bring to the fore; all cards must match the Commander’s color identity.

Wizards has a handy rundown here , but it’s become popular for a few reasons. For one, players can build around any Legendary Creature that speaks to them, either for lore reasons, because of the way they play, or just because they love the art.

It’s also the easiest way to play casual games with friends, with no real banned cards unless you agree to something beforehand. For my group, for example, we play a bunch of precons and upgraded decks that harken back to the format’s earlier days.

Finally, it’s a multiplayer format that allows a group of three friends to introduce a fourth, and so on and so forth.

There are a few reasons for this, with one of the main ones being the player count. Wizards would presumably need to make Commander’s Arena mechanics scale from 3 to at least 4 players.

Commander games can run long, too, meaning it’d need to be able to support the same game being playable for hours. It’d require a whole new deckbuilding system, too, and a way to track damage dealt by Commander cards.

Then there’s the card list. Hundreds of cards have been printed with Commander in mind, and the lack of rotation means those cards would still need to be viable. On a cynical note, Wizards of the Coast would need to work out how to earn older cards within the game’s existing ecosystem, too.

In a recent interview with YouTube creator Ashlizzlle , Senior Digital Product Manager at Wizards of the Coast, Dave Finseth discussed the possibility of Arena gaining Commander as a format.

"It's being worked on," Finseth explained, but it doesn’t sound as though it’ll come anytime soon.

"There are several challenges with adding it to the game. It's a giant task, I would say. When we built Arena, we weren't thinking this was going to be a four-player game; we were thinking, ‘how do we make Standard,' ‘how do we make Draft'.”

“There are a lot of things that we almost call ‘impossible’ design things we need to fix,” Finseth added

“They're not actually impossible, but that gives an example of how much design work and engineering work we need to do,” he added.

“I also don't know if we'll ever have all of the cards. That's not even really I don't even think the goal. It's just to get to that four-player game mode that we're targeting.“

Finseth also couldn’t commit to how Commander would integrate communication in an Arena setting, but it’s interesting to hear the discussion.

Back in 2024, Hasbro’s CEO Chris Cocks told Bloomberg that “[the company] is testing a video game version of Commander, which would potentially be separate from Arena and allow for more than two players to compete.”

Just last week , Alchemy was retired as a format in Arena, while Wizards of the Coast also confirmed that 50% of players just play Standard, while others enjoy Pioneer and Brawl. It shows that the company isn’t afraid to make big changes, but whether one of those could be integrating Commander (or spinning it out to its own client), remains to be seen.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Bungie Denies Rumor It Plans to Merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs, Confirms Marathon December and March 2027 Updates Are Free
articles.summary: Bungie has stepped in to deny a rumor that it planned to merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs amid continued questions about the future of both franchises.
articles.body:
Bungie has stepped in to deny a rumor that it planned to merge the Destiny and Marathon IPs amid continued questions about the future of both franchises.

The rumor, which has been doing the rounds online this week, was that Bungie was testing reworking Marathon and Destiny into a single IP. But, according to Marathon creative director Julia Nardin, that’s untrue.

“As someone who’s worked on both Destiny and Marathon, I can confirm that the “leak” about us merging the two IPs is fake,” Nardin said in a post on Twitter / X. “They share a lot of the same Bungie DNA, but like siblings they’re also their own independent entities. Please don’t believe everything you read online.”

It has of course been a tumultuous time for Bungie, Destiny, and Marathon. Marathon began life as an ultra hardcore extraction shooter, but Bungie has been retooling it to play more like Destiny since as the game has struggled for players. Meanwhile, Bungie stopped work on Destiny 2 to focus on Marathon — upsetting Destiny fans in the process. Livestreams from Bungie parent company Sony Interactive Entertainment have been overrun by calls for Bungie to return to the world of Destiny , either to continue with Destiny 2 or work on Destiny 3.

This week, Bungie announced a move away from seasonal content , a focus on PvE, and a significant delay for Marathon’s next update. It was slated to release on September 22, but will now arrive on December 8. A further significant update will be released in March. On October 6, Marathon will get a smaller update that resets progression and the in-game economy to prepare for an overhaul.

In a social media follow-up , Bungie clarified that the December and March updates are free, not paid DLC. “If you own Marathon, the December and March updates will be available at no additional cost,” the studio said. “That includes gameplay content such as new zones, weapons, and Runners.”

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

Which begs the question: why issue this clarification? Some believe it suggests a move to free-to-play supported by paid expansions, and these updates should not be confused with expansion-type content. However, Bungie hasn't announced any expansions for Marathon. Perhaps the plan is for different editions of Marathon, some paid, that would sit alongside a free offering. These might offer different tiers of content, allowing players to pick and choose.

The spectre in all this is of course Sony’s ongoing commitment to Marathon. It backed the game publicly, but some fans are worried about its future. Steam concurrents do not paint the full picture of a multiplatform game, but it’s worth noting that Marathon had a 24-hour peak of 2,464 on Valve’s platform, down from an all-time peak of 77,358 set when the game launched in March.
